newsitem.title: UK: EMI says confident of full-year improvement.
newsitem.headline: EMI says confident of full-year improvement.

text.p: EMI Group Plc, one of the world's leading music companies, said on Tuesday it was confident that its results for the year ending March 1997 would be better than those of last year.

"Even after taking account of the lower growth rates in some of our markets, we are confident that adjusted earnings at actual exchange rates will show an improvement on those reported for the previous year," the company said in a statement.
EMI had adjusted earnings per share of 49p last year and pre-tax profit of 367 million pounds ($597 million), excluding exceptional items.

The company, which demerged from rentals group Thorn Plc last year, said its pre-tax, pre-exceptional profits fell to 293.3 million pounds in the nine months to December 31 from 312.4 million pounds a year earlier.
EMI said its release schedule this year was weighted towards the final quarter and that it was confident of a satisfactory full year outcome.

It said that the global music market remained patchy, with the U.S. weaker than it would have liked. However, it said it was confident in the health of the music market overall in the coming years. ($1=.6142 Pound)
